comment_text:
Disclaimer: This comment has opposing views to the above presented content. I am currently doing my MTech CSE from IIT Delhi. All my view in this comment is limited to CSE and EE Dept only.

- I agree with Rahuram, the placement this year has seen a dip, but the situation was not catastrophic all the students GPA>7 got placed.  Only the range of opportunities was low. Students had less variety to choose from. 

- MS and MTech course in IITs are not same kind of programs. This video is misleading in this part. The programs are designed and operated in a very different manner in IITs. If I am not wrong Rahuram is a MS student and not MTech

- Regarding MS: 
MS is a short-term research program (3 years *varies*); in this you will spend less time in course work and more time doing research. MS is like a mini-PhD, an individual can validate if his/her personality is oriented towards research by doing this program. Many IITs (at least IIT D) allows students to convert their MS degree to PhD in mid-way. 

Since this is a research-oriented course you will spend more time in a lab under a professor (guide), your graduation depends on your guide.  You have to satisfy your guides requirement to graduate. 

Naturally student who complete this course, have an edge in joining a R&D role (real R&D not just by name) that are niche. In my department MS students get R&D jobs or go for a good PhD program in India and abroad (Top ones). Most of them are not interested in conventional placements. 

- Regarding MTech:
MTech is like a short BTech. It is a 2-year long program (4 Sem). A student has to do course work (typically 6 courses) and a MTech project (1 Year long). This program is designed for BTech students to learn some advance course and perform a rigorous project and prepare them for the industry jobs. 

Doing research in MTech is difficult, a student will not get enough time considering the heavy course work. This will be a good suite for student who want to job IITs for just the conventional placements.   

- Conclusion:
Please do not take one program just you did not get another program. This might lead to complications. If your personal goals are not aligned with the program, it will cause unnecessary friction, and make a student's master experience bad.

Enter a master's program with a clear exit plan. Take your time in analysis before joining a maters program. The program should match your goal. 

During a bachelor's program you will find many students with you aligned mindset and goals. In a maters program that is not the case, each student has his/her own background story (with/without work experience, from another department etc.) and has his/her own goals (govt job/ PhD/ Private company/ Family business), so if your goal is not clear it will create confusions. 

Happy for feedback.

comment_text:
The comparison is misleading.

The ₹1.5 Cr figure for a Harvard graduate is simply the ~$175K median starting salary converted at nominal exchange rates. But since you’d be earning and spending in the U.S., purchasing power should be compared using Purchasing Power Parity (PPP), not raw conversion rates.

When adjusted for PPP, IIM Ahmedabad’s ₹36L salary offers a similar standard of living in India as $175K does in the U.S. (Direct conversion of ₹36L in India using a PPP converter - ~$176K)

So, regardless of where you graduate from, your lifestyle tends to align with the local economy - not the currency exchange rate. Ofc, IIMA is no Harvard in terms of prestige and earning in USD will help a lot - but the lifestyle/salary factor is misrepresented here.

Honestly, as it stands today, the biggest problem that works against choosing Harvard is the current situation for immigrants in the US.

comment_text: Points to Note: 1. Placement Report Not Audited. 2. Mckinsey didn't come for Final Placements. 3. The companies listed will operate in Transformational or Operational consulting. So those Jobs are no where comparable to MBB Consulting jobs. 4. No Bulge Bracket Investment banks + No Major PE fund or VC fund. Almost all the roles offered are Commercial banking roles + Relationship manager roles + credit manager roles. Crux : Its a Good college with decent placement Report, but don't be under the Illusion that you will get in MBB consulting or Front end IB roles or PE/VC Analyst Roles.

comment_text:
Bhai, seedhi baat bolta hu. Tera profile mixed hai, weak bhi hai aur strong bhi.

* 10th theek hai, but 12th (68%) is below par
* 3 saal gap is a red flag for many companies
* Tier 3 se neeche college campus placements weak rahenge

Strong points:

* CA Foundation + Inter cleared (that too with grad) is big plus
* 9 CGPA expected is strong recovery
* OBC + non-engineer toh CAT me advantage
* Direct campus se 30+ LPA rare hai even in top B-schools. Only top roles (IB, consulting, PE) wo bhi top 5–10% logon ko milta hai.

But impossible nahi hai. Bas path alag hoga.

1. CAT pe all-in ja
* Target: 99+ percentile
* Aim: BLACKI / FMS / SPJIMR level college

2. Finance me jaana hai toh: CA Inter is gold so use it properly
Start:
  * Financial modeling
  * Excel + valuation
  * Basic accounting strong kar

3. Random exams (JAM, GATE, TIFR) sirf CV bharne ke liye mat de
* Recruiters ko samajh aa jata hai “directionless banda”
* Pick ONE path: MBA (Finance)

Achha package possible hai, but straight nahi milega. CAT me 99+ la, top college le, finance skills build kar, phir top roles target kar. Random exams se CV bharne ke chakkar me mat pad, direction clear rakh.

Program type: Full-time MBA (12–24 months) ya Executive MBA (part-time, 18–24 months). Agar fresh graduate ho, toh full-time jaana better hota hai.


2. Entry Requirements:

Degree: Bachelor’s ya equivalent (minimum 3 saal)

Work Experience: Full-time work experience 2 se 3 saal helpful hoti hai, lekin kuch schools freshers ke liye bhi intakes rakhte hain.

Tests: GMAT (minimum 550 to 600) ya GRE (300+). Kuch schools English proficiency (IELTS 6.5+/TOEFL 90+) bhi maangte hain.


3. Application Timeline:

Rounds: Generally 3 to 4 rounds, pehla Jan–Feb mein, last tak June–July.

Documents: Transcripts, CV, SOP, 2 letters of recommendation, test scores, passport copy.


4. Fees & Funding:

Tuition: €30,000–€40,000 total.

Living Cost: €900–1,200/month (rent + groceries + transport)

Scholarships: DAAD Scholarships, university-specific merit scholarships (up to 50% fee waiver), or Deutschlandstipendium

Student Loan: Indian banks ke education loans yahan cover karte hain — collateral-based & unsecured options available


5. Visa & Work:

Student Visa: Initial 24 months ya program length ke liye

Post-Study Work: Graduation ke baad 18 mahine ka “Job-Seeker Visa” milta hai. Uske andar full-time job search karke Blue Card milta hai


6. Resources & Platforms:

Apply: University websites directly, ya platforms like Study in Germany (study-in-germany.de) se official guidance!

Community: LinkedIn pe “Indian MBA Germany” groups, WhatsApp/Telegram communities se networking shuru kar do aap!


Agar koi specific program ya city me interest ho, batao — exact admission deadlines aur scholarship deadlines share kar dunga!

എല്ലാവർക്കും ഹോസ്റ്റൽ കിട്ടും എന്നത് ശരിയാണ് പക്ഷെ ആദ്യം വരുന്ന കുട്ടികൾക്ക് ആയിരിക്കും rooms കിട്ടാൻ സാധ്യത. കുറച്ച് കുട്ടികൾക്ക് ആദ്യത്തെ സെമസ്റ്ററിൽ hostels ഇലെ dorms ഇൽ നിൽക്കേണ്ടി വന്ന സാഹചര്യം ഈ വർഷങ്ങളിൽ ഉണ്ടായിട്ടുണ്ട്. (99 ശതമാനവും റൂം കിട്ടും) 

Hostel room rent എന്നത് boys നും girlsനും ഒരു വർഷത്തിൽ 900 രൂപ ആണ്. (Girls ന് ഈ വർഷം മുതലാണ് പൈസ വന്നത് , മുമ്പ് സൗജന്യമായിരുന്നു.) മെസ് ഫീസ് ഒരു സെമസ്റ്ററിൽ 10-15k വരും. ഹോസ്റ്റൽ റൂം മാത്രമായി കിട്ടില്ല, മെസും എടുക്കണം. 

പിന്നെ ക്യാമ്പസ് അത്യാവശ്യം vibrant ആണ്. എപ്പോഴും എന്തെങ്കിലും ഒക്കെ പരിപാടികൾ ഉണ്ടാകും. Academics ന്റെ കാര്യത്തിലേക്ക് വന്നാൽ department നോക്കി മാത്രം വരിക. യൂണിവേഴ്‌സിറ്റി കണ്ട് വന്നാൽ നിരാശയാകും. 

ചില department നല്ല acadmeics തരുന്ന department തന്നെയാണ്. യൂണിവേഴ്‌സിറ്റിയിലെ  പല departments നെ കുറിച്ചും മോശം അഭിപ്രായങ്ങൾ കേട്ടിട്ടുണ്ട്. 

നാട്ടിൽ നിന്നും ഇവിടെ എത്താൻ  മലബാർ area ഇൽ ഉള്ളവർക്ക് എല്ലാ വെള്ളിയാഴ്ച യും ഞായറാഴ്ചയും direct ട്രെയിൻ ഉണ്ട്. (16856 - മംഗലാപുരം പുതുച്ചേരി എക്സ്പ്രസ്). കോഴിക്കോട്- ഷൊർണ്ണൂർ- പാലക്കാട് വഴി, കോഴിക്കോട് നിന്ന് K swift ബസും daily സർവീസ് ഉണ്ട്.

തെക്കൻ കേരളത്തിൽ നിന്ന് ആണെങ്കിൽ പോണ്ടിച്ചേരിയിൽ നിന്ന് ഒരു മണിക്കൂർ ദൂരം സഞ്ചരിച്ചാൽ എത്തുന്ന വില്ലുപുരത്തേക്ക് ട്രയിൻ ഉണ്ട്. (അനന്തപുരി എക്സ്പ്രസ്, കൊല്ലം എക്സ്പ്രസ്) , കൂടാതെ തിരുവനന്തപുരത്ത് നിന്ന് തമിഴ്നാട് RTC യുടെ ബസ് daily സർവീസ് ഉണ്ട്, private bus ഉം ഉണ്ട്. 
മധ്യ കേരളത്തിൽ നിന്ന് ആണെകിൽ private buses and  വില്ലുപ്പുരം ട്രെയിൻസ്‌ ഉണ്ട്.

comment_text: Honestly the professors are really good at teaching. Regular seminars are also conducted and you get a chance to learn and communicate with foreign professors and archaeologist who visit there. I still remember seeing the excavation process and technical tools demonstrated by UK archaeologist. The professors are very strict, they take attendance very seriously.  There is also a department library. We only got study materials for the 1st semester, for the rest we had to rely on lecture notes that you take and numerous books from the library. There is no one book, you have to go through several books. Also the third year projects are nerve-wracking. Try to think about topics for the project since second year itself and talk to your preferred professor early on or else you will have to settle with whoever is remaining.Overall it a nice and quiet environment. And one more thing, the Archaeology dept. Is not fun unlike the others. During my time, the only fun activity was freshers and farewell. I used to go to other facilities for trips, competitions and other activities. You wouldn't hear a sound in our dept. 😂 Academically it is very nice. If you have any doubts feel free to ask me.

comment_text:
चंडीगढ़ यूनिवर्सिटी – चमक ज्यादा, सच्चाई कम?
Chandigarh University का नाम बड़े-बड़े विज्ञापनों और NIRF रैंकिंग के कारण बहुत सुनाई देता है। लेकिन असली सवाल यह है — क्या छात्रों को पूरी सच्चाई बताई जाती है?
बीटेक (कंप्यूटर साइंस) की 4 साल की कुल फीस लगभग 18 लाख रुपये तक पहुंच जाती है। हॉस्टल, अन्य चार्ज और खर्च अलग। यानी कुल खर्च 20 लाख के आसपास बैठ सकता है।
और बदले में औसतन प्लेसमेंट पैकेज बताया जाता है लगभग 5–6 लाख रुपये सालाना।
अब सीधी बात —
अगर 18 लाख खर्च करके 5–6 लाख की नौकरी मिले, तो क्या यह समझदारी है या सिर्फ ब्रांड के नाम का भ्रम?
सबसे बड़ा सवाल – पारदर्शिता क्यों नहीं?
वेबसाइट पर एक आंकड़ा
सरकारी रिपोर्ट में दूसरा आंकड़ा
फोन पर पूछो तो कंपनी-वाइज लिस्ट देने में हिचकिचाहट
अगर सब कुछ साफ है, तो पूरी प्लेसमेंट लिस्ट सार्वजनिक क्यों नहीं?
पढ़ाई कम, प्रचार ज्यादा?
कई छात्रों की राय है कि यहां पढ़ाई से ज्यादा इवेंट, शो, फंक्शन और प्रचार पर ध्यान दिया जाता है। कैंपस चमकदार है, विज्ञापन दमदार है — लेकिन असली दम प्लेसमेंट क्वालिटी में दिखना चाहिए, न कि सिर्फ होर्डिंग और यूट्यूब एड में।
मेरे देश के छात्रों और माता-पिता के लिए संदेश
⚠️ बड़ी यूनिवर्सिटी का नाम = बड़ी सफलता नहीं होता।
⚠️ विज्ञापन देखकर एडमिशन लेना सबसे बड़ी गलती हो सकती है।
⚠️ 18–20 लाख रुपये कोई छोटी रकम नहीं है।
एडमिशन लेने से पहले यह मांगें:
✔ कंपनी-वाइज प्लेसमेंट लिस्ट
✔ मीडियन पैकेज (सिर्फ हाईएस्ट नहीं)
✔ कुल खर्च का साफ हिसाब
✔ पिछले 3 साल का असली डेटा
माता-पिता की मेहनत की कमाई को सिर्फ ब्रांड के नाम पर दांव पर मत लगाइए।

comment_text:
No doubt Manipal is expensive. Studied here way back in 2007-2011. But so were other private colleges who were equally expensive or even more. So singling out Manipal for being expensive will be like ignoring all other expensive colleges in India. We have schools who are expensive in India as well. Problem is the population where a lot of 12th passed churn out every year. Where do they go if engineering is their choice. IIT NIT to milna nahi sab ko. Reservation alag hai. That is where Private colleges come in. 
Manipal does justice. You come out a better person after studying here. You get good infra and good facilities. Safe and ragging free culture. Fees is a personal thing. If you can pay it, you will join anywhere if you want to study there or be part of a certain college.

Also thanks for pointing out obvious things and not being totally biased about those.

comment_text:
I'm currently a 3rd-year student at Bennett University, and if you're considering taking admission here — think twice. Here’s why:

1. The campus is small and dull. You’ll get bored within the first 48 hours. There’s barely anything to explore or engage with.


2. The grading system makes no sense. I scored 85 in a subject and still ended up with a C+ — zero transparency, and absolutely demotivating.


3. Many top companies have already blacklisted Bennett. Placement opportunities shrink fast once you realize who won’t even show up.


4. Yes, it’s better than AKTU — but that’s a low bar. Don’t confuse “better than bad” with “actually good.”


5. The food is shockingly bad. It’s honestly questionable whether even animals would eat it. You’ll end up surviving on Maggi and outside junk.


6. Lectures? Prepare to be bored to death. Most classes feel like they're just reading slides with no real engagement or value.


7. There are a lot of things more but in short just don't take admission here,




---

Final word: If you're serious about your education, career, and experience — explore other options. Bennett sells a dream, but most of us end up waking up disappointed.

comment_text:
Final Year Student Review – Overall Not Recommended

01. Hostels: 2.5/5
A: Showers often stop working mid-use; once got stuck in the toilet during a water outage.

02. Mess: 1/5
A: Very poor food quality. Typically two curries, roti, rice, and a watery sweet dish. During monsoon, insects and even a frog were reportedly found in the food.

03. Transport: 3/5
A: Initially provided buses to classes, but services were later discontinued.

04. Classrooms: 4/5
A: Seats are all on the same level; should be tiered for better visibility. New campuses have this, most older ones don’t.

05. Dating: 5/5
A: No restrictions. Around 30% of students find partners here.

06. Freedom: 5/5
A: Full freedom. Unlimited Wi-Fi and no surveillance.

07. Care: 5/5
A: Wardens are caring and attentive, even toward introverts. Mentors are helpful.

08. Faculties: 1/5
A: Teaching quality is poor; most just read directly from PowerPoint slides.

09. Hygiene: 1/5
A: Strong gutter smell and unhygienic street food around the campus.

10. Management: 1/5
A: Despite having biometric attendance, they still rely on outdated paper logs for hostel entry and exit.

Overall Verdict: Not recommended

comment_text: The reality is far away from this . The batch size has gone over 800  students. Forget about the placements , getting a summer placement is a huge task . If one knows basic mathematics , average can easily go up over 25 lakhs even if 20  percent of the students get packages upwards of 25 lakhs per anum.. What about the rest . The fees mentioned on the website is around 25 lakhs. That does not includes the hostel. They do not provide on campus hostels . The residence which they provide is priced at around 3 lakh for 10 months .This does not includes mess charges . The expenses adds up to upwards of 35 lakhs with no guarantee of placements. The loan covers only around 25 lakhs. Above which one has to risk giving security . If you belong to a middle class background and are dependent on loan for your MBA , be aware of the pros and cons before making any decision . There are way better colleges. The most important thing is looking at the ROI of a B school especially if you belong to a middle class background.

Graphic Era University’s so-called Scholarship Exam *GECET* is a complete scam – BEWARE!

Let me save you of the trouble you are heading yourself into if thinking of taking admission in this university and tell you straight: Graphic Era University’s scholarship exam is an absolute joke and a disgusting money-making scam. They lure students with flashy promises of "up to 100% scholarships" and create this whole image of being a supportive, merit-based institution. But the truth? It’s just a clever way for them to loot ₹1500 from thousands of students with zero intention of actually awarding anything to anyone.

I paid the ₹1500 registration fee, studied seriously, and took the exam with full hope. But guess what? The exam was scheduled on 20th April and the results were released on 4th May which stated I have not qualified..how stupid..who fails in an online proctored exam right!!.If not a full scholarship, at least 70–80% should be justified. It's hard to believe anyone would be considered not qualified—it feels like they just don’t want to give it at all.

When you try contacting them, they either ignore you completely or give you robotic, copy-paste responses — as if you're just a number to them. And then the cherry on top? They conveniently mark you as “ineligible” without showing a single mark or explaining anything. On enquiring multiple times about the process of allotment of scholarship, eligibility criteria or a question as simple as "what is my damn score"..they will tell you there is no data for the cbt mode exams and the rest is confidential...they will keep asking you to post mails on different id and the loop never ends. How is that even fair or professional? Above all this is the audacity to tell the candidate to re-appear for the exam in the next phase by paying another 1500 and making a fool out of themselves. It’s obvious this is just a cash-grab operation. 

Honestly, it’s shameful that a university claiming to be “prestigious” is running such a shady scheme. If they can deceive students before admission, imagine what else they’ll lie about after you join. If this is how they treat students who haven’t even enrolled yet, I can’t even imagine the mess they make once you’re trapped inside.

My advice: stay FAR away from Graphic Era University. There are plenty of other colleges that are honest, transparent, and actually care about students. Don’t fall for the fake promises and shiny ads — this place is all about money, not education.

To the university: Stop calling yourself “Graphic Era” and start calling yourself “Loot Era.” At least then people will know what they’re getting into.

Let me save you of the trouble you are heading yourself into if thinking of taking admission in this university and tell you straight: Graphic Era University’s scholarship exam is an absolute joke and a disgusting money-making scam. They lure students with flashy promises of "up to 100% scholarships" and create this whole image of being a supportive, merit-based institution. But the truth? How is that even fair or professional? Above all this is the audacity to tell the candidate to re-appear for the exam in the next phase by paying another 1500 and making a fool out of themselves. It’s obvious this is just a cash-grab operation. 

Honestly, it’s shameful that a university claiming to be “prestigious” is running such a shady scheme. If they can deceive students before admission, imagine what else they’ll lie about after you join. If this is how they treat students who haven’t even enrolled yet, I can’t even imagine the mess they make once you’re trapped inside.

My advice: stay FAR away from Graphic Era University. There are plenty of other colleges that are honest, transparent, and actually care about students. Don’t fall for the fake promises and shiny ads — this place is all about money, not education.

To the university: Stop calling yourself “Graphic Era” and start calling yourself “Loot Era.” At least then people will know what they’re getting into.

I’m a student from the 2021–2025 batch at SASTRA, and I want to share my honest experience—especially for students coming from North India. If you are getting CSE or any branch under the School of Computing, you will likely get placed with a salary between 3 to 4 LPA if you’re an average student. Also, placements are not good if you are from non-computing branches like ECE. There’s a big gap between computing and other branches. The placement data shown in video is of 2024 passing out batch. The branchwise data shown in video is not from official source but from one of the trusted source "college pravesh" as official source have not mentioned branchwise statistics. 

But to give an idea that the mentioned brachwise data of 2024 batch is close to reality I have mentioned 2 official placement data by institute:
NIRF Report: https://www.iiita.ac.in/uploads/20250116-NIRF%20(Engineering)%202025%20Submitted%20Report914.pdf
Official Institute Website (Check 2023-24 data): https://placement.iiita.ac.in/placementStatistic.html

comment_text:
Worst college. I repeat, worst college to join. Don’t ever come here.

80% attendance rule. Disciplinary action for little things. No night campus culture. Still have to take outpass for going out and have to return by 7 PM.

Have to go to hostel by 9:30 PM. They don’t allow students to play games outside the hostel after 9:40 PM.

Hostel rooms have metal mesh in the balcony so that students cannot look out.

Worst mess food. You will pay mess fees for food but cannot eat there. Zomato is the option.

Worst management. Director and registrar are the worst. They don’t give funds for student projects, fests, and other events.

Faculties are very strict about attendance. If you fall below the 80% attendance mark, they collect ₹1000 for every 1% shortage.

Fake placement report. There were only 30% placements, but they are claiming 100%. No core placements.

Very, very poor college.

If you want good placements, a memorable college life, and a strong alumni base, then please avoid this college.

As a student/victim of this college with 95 percentile in JEE, I am saying this.

They care only about professors and their research groups.

बिट्स पिलानी और मैसाचुसेट्स इंस्टीट्यूट ऑफ टेक्नोलॉजी (MIT) की तुलना करें तो यह स्पष्ट होता है कि शोध, नवाचार और वैश्विक प्रभाव के मामले में बिट्स बहुत पीछे है। MIT लगातार QS और THE (Times Higher Education) रैंकिंग में टॉप 5 में बना रहता है, जबकि बिट्स पिलानी 800-1000 की रैंकिंग में आता है। शोध और गुणवत्ता के मामले में भी MIT बहुत आगे है, जिसके 100 से अधिक नोबेल पुरस्कार विजेता हैं, जबकि बिट्स से अभी तक कोई भी वैज्ञानिक इस स्तर तक नहीं पहुंच पाया है। पेटेंट और औद्योगिक नवाचारों में भी MIT हर साल हजारों पेटेंट फाइल करता है, जबकि बिट्स इस मामले में बहुत पीछे है। IITs फिर भी किसी हद तक वैश्विक स्तर पर अपनी पहचान बना रहे हैं, लेकिन बिट्स पिलानी जैसे संस्थानों की स्थिति और भी कमजोर है।

यह और भी शर्मनाक तब हो जाता है जब तथाकथित "मेरिट" का रोना रोने वाले लोग शिक्षा प्रणाली में मौजूद अन्याय को नजरअंदाज करते हैं। बिट्स पिलानी में एडमिशन के लिए 24-25 लाख रुपए की भारी-भरकम फीस और इसके पहले कोचिंग संस्थानों में लाखों रुपए बर्बाद करने के बावजूद भी यह संस्थान MIT से कोसों दूर है। यह वही "अंगूठा काटो" नीति है, जिसमें सिर्फ पैसे और संसाधनों तक सीमित लोगों को ही आगे बढ़ने का मौका दिया जाता है, जबकि भारत की अधिकांश जनता को उच्च शिक्षा से बाहर कर दिया जाता है। MIT जैसे संस्थान जहाँ स्कॉलरशिप और रिसर्च फंडिंग से प्रतिभाओं को बढ़ावा देते हैं, वहीं भारत में महंगी फीस और कोचिंग इंडस्ट्री का जाल अधिकांश योग्य छात्रों को आगे बढ़ने से रोक देता है। ऐसी व्यवस्था पर गर्व करने वालों को यह सोचना चाहिए कि जब इतने संसाधनों और अवसरों के बाद भी बिट्स पिलानी MIT से इतना पीछे है, तो यह "मेरिट" की जीत नहीं बल्कि एक असफलता की कहानी है।

comment_text:
I am a B.Pharm graduate from BIT Mesra. Based on my experience, I do not recommend taking admission to this college, as I found it to be a poor return on investment. I spent around 16 lakhs in fees, but the college did not bring a single company for campus placements in my course. This issue is not limited to B.Pharm-other courses also face similar placement challenges. The placement brochure and NAAC accreditation do not reflect the actual situation, and I found them to be of little value.

The college seems more focused on collecting money, often imposing heavy fines, rather than supporting students' futures. In my opinion, spending 15–18 lakhs here is not justified, especially when you can complete your course at a reputable college for 6–8 lakhs. The so-called fame of BIT Mesra is also overrated in regions like North and West India, most people confuse BIT Mesra with BITS Pilani and are not aware of this institution.

My honest advice is to consider other colleges that offer better value for your money and genuine placement support.
